tools.name: create_account
tools.description: Open a Glide account for a person. Returns their wallets immediately — Base and Solana, both able to receive USDC and both x402-payable — with no verification and no fee. Also returns a verification link, which is optional and only needed for bank rails (a US account, USD, EUR and other currencies);

tools.name: check_status
tools.description: Where the person is in bank verification: awaiting_verification, in_review, approved or declined. Call this after they open the verification link — approval usually takes about two minutes. Their wallets already work regardless of what this says.

tools.name: get_funding_details
tools.description: The US bank account — account number and routing number — plus the USDC address on Base. This is the banking half, so it needs verification to be approved; before that it refuses. On and off ramps are free. For a wallet address that works right now, without verification, use get_wallets.

tools.name: get_wallets
tools.description: The person's Base and Solana wallet addresses, plus the x402 endpoint on each chain that lets any agent pay them in USDC. Works from the moment the account exists: no verification, no fee, nothing to set up. Receiving is free and unlimited; moving the balance into a US or EUR bank account is the par

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_account · Private data: get_funding_details, get_wallets · Public sink: create_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_account · Private data: get_funding_details, get_wallets · Public sink: create_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
